chunks: Via types and their tradeoffs. The question: What are the different types of vias? What are their tradeoffs?
There are four main kinds of via. A through via runs from the top of the board to the bottom. A blind via starts on an outer layer and stops inside.
A buried via connects inner layers only. A microvia is a tiny laser-drilled hole spanning one layer. Through vias are the cheapest and most robust.
The others save space or shorten stubs, but they cost more, so use through vias unless something forces you not to.
Think of a building. A stairwell that runs through every floor is a through via. It is cheap, but it uses space on every floor.
A staircase from the lobby to the second floor is a blind via. A staircase between two upper floors is a buried via. A short ladder between neighboring floors is a microvia.
Each via spans a different layer range. The buried via leaves both outer surfaces free.
The through via on the right is used only from L1 to L3, so the red lower barrel is an unused stub that rings at its quarter-wave frequency.
Through via: drilled through the whole board. Blind via: connects an outer layer to an inner layer and stops there.
Buried via: connects inner layers and is invisible from both outer surfaces. Microvia: a very small laser-drilled via that spans a single layer.
It lets chips with tightly packed pins route their wires out. Stub: the unused part of a through via barrel below the layer where the signal exits.
Say a fast signal goes from the top layer to an inner layer through a through via. The part of the barrel below the exit is a stub.
A stub rings at the frequency where it is a quarter of a wavelength long, c over (4 square root of r ) .
A 3 mm stub in typical board material rings near 12 gigahertz, a problem for a 25 Gb/s link (25 billion bits per second). A blind via or microvia has almost no stub.
But blind and buried vias need extra build steps, which cost money. That is the whole idea: through vias are the default, and the other kinds trade cost for density.

"The main types are through vias, which go top to bottom and are cheapest; blind vias, which go from an outer layer to an inner one; buried vias, which connect inner layers only; and microvias, which are tiny laser-drilled vias spanning one layer, sometimes stacked.

The tradeoff is cost and complexity against density and signal integrity: blind, buried and micro need extra lamination or laser steps, so I default to through vias and only go further when BGA pitch, layer count or stub resonance forces it."
